anchors.prompt: Explain how a memory-bound decode step differs from a compute-bound one.
anchors.text:
A memory-bound decode step is one where the performance is limited by the speed at which data can be read from memory, whereas a compute-bound step is limited by the processing power of the CPU. In a memory-bound step, the CPU spends more time waiting for data than computing, while in a compute-bound step, the CPU is fully utilized in processing data.
